HubSpot Company Record — LuminaAI (ID: 10488)

Account summary
- Building AI-assisted support workflows embedded in their SaaS (agent + summarization + retrieval). Primary pain: inference spend is growing faster than revenue; wants predictable unit economics.
- Interested in Redwood primarily for serving consistency + cost controls (batching/caching) without re-architecting.
- Likely deployment: VPC (customer data sensitivity); may start hosted for prototyping but expects VPC for production.

Stage notes (evaluation / POC scoping)
- They are not shopping for “best model”; they are shopping for predictable $/ticket and stable latency at peak hours.
- Quote from call: “We can live with slightly higher latency as long as it’s consistent and we don’t get timeouts.”
- Strong interest in workload-aware batching defaults; asked specifically about what ‘cost-efficient’ does to streaming cadence.

Key activities (recent)
- 2025-02-28: Fireflies POC scoping call (ff-2025-02-28-luminaai-poc-scoping). Attendees: Lumina Eng lead + PM; Redwood: Miguel Santos (AE), Henry Cho (SE).
- 2025-03-01: Sent POC proposal + tier overview + questions on routing/regions (Gmail thread: thread-20250301T165902Z-luminaai-poc-proposal).
- 2025-03-12: Internal sync w/ runtime/product on how to position batching tiers + “effective config” visibility for POC debugging.
- 2025-03-18: Lumina confirmed they can run canary traffic through a single endpoint and tag requests by route/tier for comparison.

Workload details (from scoping)
- Routes
  - Chat: customer-facing assistant, streaming responses required (token cadence matters).
  - Summarization: non-streaming, batch-friendly, mostly background jobs.
  - Retrieval: embeddings + reranking; latency is important but can be async for some flows.
- Prompt/profile characteristics
  - Chat prompts often 1–4k tokens (multi-turn + policies); occasional long-context spikes.
  - Concurrency spikes at top-of-hour (support shift changes) + product launches.
- Reliability constraints
  - They’d rather shed load / degrade gracefully than stall (requested clear overload behavior).

Deployment + security constraints
- Must run in their VPC for production (data handling policy). Hosted ok for early testing but not for customer data.
- Requirements called out:
  - SSO/SAML for Console access.
  - Audit logs for config changes (esp. changes to batching tier / defaults).
  - Retention controls for logs/metrics. Prefer KMS integration.
- Region: US (initial). EU later.

POC goals / success criteria (as stated)
- Primary: reduce inference cost meaningfully without harming UX.
  - Target: 15–25% lower $/1M tokens on summarization + back-office workloads using cost-efficient tier.
- Latency SLOs (initial POC targets)
  - Chat (streaming): p95 time-to-first-token ≤ 450ms; token cadence shouldn’t “stall” (they measure gaps > ~250–300ms as bad UX).
  - Summarization (non-streaming): p95 end-to-end ≤ 2.5s at their expected prompt size distribution.
  - Error/timeout: no increase vs baseline; explicitly watching cancellation/timeout rate under cost-efficient.
- Observability requirements
  - Wants to see queue delay and batch formation stats per tier (asked for “what batch size did I actually get?”).
  - Requested a way to view “effective batching config” (tier defaults vs overrides) for debugging.

Batching tier positioning for Lumina (current recommendation)
- Chat / streaming: start with standard tier; only move to fast if TTFT misses, and only use cost-efficient after cadence is validated.
- Summarization + offline jobs: cost-efficient tier default candidate (with guardrails on queue delay + overload protection).
- Retrieval (reranking): depends on concurrency; likely standard first.

POC plan (draft)
- Week 1
  - Deploy in Lumina VPC sandbox.
  - Establish baseline with standard tier across key routes.
- Week 2
  - Enable cost-efficient tier for summarization route only (canary 10% → 50% → 100%).
  - Compare: p95 latency, queue delay, batch size distribution, GPU util, and $/token.
- Go/no-go
  - If timeouts/cancels increase or streaming cadence regression is observed, pause rollout and revert to standard.

Open questions / risks
- Streaming cadence sensitivity: they are worried cost-efficient tier may introduce perceptible pauses.
- Long-context outliers: asked what happens when a 16k+ context request lands during peak concurrency.
- “Tier vs explicit overrides” confusion: they want overrides for max queue delay on a per-route basis but don’t want to lose tier guardrails.

Next steps (owner + dates)
- Redwood (Henry Cho): send concrete config examples by route (standard vs cost-efficient) + what can be overridden safely (ETA: 2025-03-20).
- Redwood (Miguel Santos): align security questionnaire items for VPC deployment + audit logs/retention docs (ETA: 2025-03-22).
- Lumina: provide 24h traffic shape summary (concurrency + prompt length histogram) and initial model preference list (ETA: 2025-03-21).
- Joint: schedule POC kickoff and decide canary cohort + success thresholds (target week of 2025-03-24).

Internal note
- This account will be a good design partner for workload-aware batching defaults (especially streaming cadence + per-route tier selection). They’re cost-driven but pragmatic, and they asked for the exact telemetry we’re building (queue delay, batch formation, effective config). Keep them close as we firm up customer-facing tier copy.
